Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?","## TL;DR
*The shield layers that come with the “OSM Bright” / “OSM Liberty” OpenMapTiles styles look for the following sprite-image IDs*
`ref_length` is an integer **1 – 6** (the style only defines badges for those lengths).
If any of those IDs are missing from the sprite sheet you will see the “bare number” symptom you described.
### How to make the badges appear **without touching the style layers**
1. **Use a sprite sheet that already contains the needed IDs**
* The official OpenMapTiles sprite for the OSM Bright style already ships all of them:
https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite
* The same sprite (identical content) is also available at the demo host:
https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite
Point your style’s `sprite` property at one of those URLs (or at a copy you host yourself).
Example style root:
```json
""version"": 8,
""sprite"": ""https://your.cdn.com/sprites/osm-bright"",
*Make sure the URL is **extension-less** – MapLibre will request `.json`, `.png`, and the `@2x` variants automatically.*
2. **If you already have a custom sprite and just need the missing badge images**
* **Option A – add a second sprite sheet** (MapLibre ≥ 3.0).
```json
""sprite"": [
{ ""id"": ""default"", ""url"": ""https://your.cdn.com/sprites/your-custom"" },
{ ""id"": ""osm-badges"", ""url"": ""https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite"" }
Then reference the badge images with the `id:` prefix, e.g. `""icon-image"": ""osm-badges:us-interstate_2""`.
*If you do **not** want to edit the layers*, keep the original `icon-image` values (`us-interstate_2`, …) and make the **default** sheet the one that contains the badges.
To do that, simply replace your current `sprite` string with the badge sprite URL (or host a merged sprite that contains both your custom icons **and** the badge IDs).
* **Option B – merge the missing IDs into your own sprite**
1. Download the OpenMapTiles sprite (`sprite.json` + `sprite.png` + `sprite@2x.png`).
2. Use a sprite-building tool (e.g. **spritezero**, **spreet**, or **Martin**) to add the badge PNGs (`us-interstate_1.png`, …, `road_6.png`) to your existing set.
3. Host the new combined sprite and point `sprite` at its base URL.
3. **If you cannot host a new sprite sheet** (e.g. you are on a strict CDN that only serves your own assets) you can register the missing images at runtime:
```js

try {
const { data } = await map.loadImage(badgeUrl);
if (!map.hasImage(id)) map.addImage(id, data);
} catch (err) {
console.warn('Could not load shield badge', id, err);

This works because `styleimagemissing` is emitted **after** the style has been parsed but **before** the layer is rendered. The handler loads the missing PNG and registers it under the same ID, so the layer instantly gets its badge back. No style changes are required.

column1: The **`ref_length`** field is an integer that tells the style how many digits the route number has (1 – 6). The sprite therefore must contain an entry for every length you expect to see.
If those IDs are missing from the style’s sprite sheet you will see the numbers (text) but no badge – exactly the symptom you described.
## 1. What the style actually asks for
### OSM Bright (the most common OpenMapTiles style)
```json
""id"": ""highway-shield-us-interstate"",
""type"": ""symbol"",
""source"": ""openmaptiles"",
""source-layer"": ""transportation_name"",
""layout"": {
""icon-image"": ""{network}_{ref_length}"",
""text-field"": ""{ref}""
* `icon-image` is an **expression** that expands to one of the four patterns above.
* When `network` = `""us-interstate""` and `ref_length` = `3` the resolved ID is **`us-interstate_3`**.
The same pattern is used for the other US networks (`us-highway`, `us-state`).
For everything else the style falls back to the generic pattern `road_<ref_length>`.
### OSM Liberty (the “default” OpenMapTiles style)
```json
""id"": ""shield"",
""type"": ""symbol"",
""source"": ""openmaptiles"",
""source-layer"": ""transportation_name"",
""layout"": {
""icon-image"": ""default_{ref_length}"",
""text-field"": ""{ref}""
*All* shields use the `default_<ref_length>` IDs, regardless of `network`.

column1: > **Note** – The *official* OSM Bright sprite that ships with the OpenMapTiles demo contains only the IDs that are actually used in the United States:
> * `us-interstate_1` – `us-interstate_3`
> * `us-highway_1` – `us-highway_3`
> * `us-state_1` – `us-state_6`
> * `road_1` – `road_6`
If you are rendering a region that needs a badge for a 4-, 5- or 6-digit US-interstate number you will have to add those images yourself (or use a custom sprite that already contains them).
## 3. Getting the badges to appear **without touching the style layers**
You have three practical ways to supply the missing sprite IDs:
### A. Point the style at a sprite sheet that already contains them
1. **Use the official OSM Bright sprite** (or the OSM Liberty sprite) as-is.
```json
""sprite"": ""https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite""
*Do not use this in production – it’s a public demo endpoint.*
2. **Self-host the same sprite** (recommended for production).
* Download the sprite directory from the OpenMapTiles repo:
`https://github.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style/tree/master/sprite`
* Host the two files (`sprite.png`, `sprite.json`) (and the `@2x` variants) on a domain you control.
* Update the style’s `sprite` property to the base URL of your host, e.g.
```json
{ ""sprite"": ""https://my.cdn.com/tiles/osm-bright/sprite"" }

3. **If you already have a custom sprite for your own icons**, you can **add a second sheet** (MapLibre ≥ 3.0) that contains the shield IDs, leaving your own sheet as `default` or vice-versa. Example:
```json
""sprite"": [
{ ""id"": ""default"", ""url"": ""https://my.cdn.com/tiles/my-icons/sprite"" },
{ ""id"": ""osm-shields"", ""url"": ""https://my.cdn.com/tiles/osm-bright/sprite"" }
Then reference the shield IDs with the prefix `osm-shields:` **only if you need to**.
Because the `default` sheet is still the first entry, **all existing `icon-image` values in the style keep working unchanged** – you do **not** have to edit any layer.
### B. Add the missing images at runtime with `addImage`
If you cannot change the `sprite` URL (e.g., you are consuming a third-party style that you cannot edit), you can register the missing badge images yourself after the map loads:
```js
map.on('load', async () => {
// Helper to load a PNG (or WebP) from a URL and add it under the exact ID the style expects
async function addBadge(id, url) {
if (map.hasImage(id)) return;               // already present
const { data } = await map.loadImage(url);  // returns an ImageBitmap / HTMLImageElement
map.addImage(id, data, { sdf: false });     // most shield badges are ordinary PNGs
// Example: add the three US-interstate badge sizes
await Promise.all([
addBadge('us-interstate_1', 'https://my.cdn.com/shields/us-interstate_1.png'),
addBadge('us-interstate_2', 'https://my.cdn.com/shields/us-interstate_2.png'),
addBadge('us-interstate_3', 'https://my.cdn.com/shields/us-interstate_3.png')
// Do the same for highway, state, and generic road badges as needed
*Pros*: No need to rebuild a sprite; you can host each badge as a tiny PNG (or even an SVG rasterised to a bitmap).
*Cons*: Each `addImage` triggers a separate HTTP request, so for many badge sizes it is a bit less efficient than a single sprite PNG/JSON pair.
### C. Use the v6 “missing-image resolver”
MapLibre v6+ provides a hook that is called **whenever the style asks for an image that does not exist**. You can supply the image on-the-fly:
```js
map.setMissingStyleImageResolver(async (id) => {
// `id` will be something like ""us-interstate_2""
const url = `https://my.cdn.com/shields/${id}.png`;
const { data } = await map.loadImage(url);
return { data, options: {} };   // same shape as Map.addImage() expects
This approach is the cleanest if you want a single place to serve *any* missing badge without pre-checking `hasImage`.
## 4. Quick checklist – “Why are my shields missing?”

column3: `style.sprite` points to a base URL **without** `.json` or `.png`.
`…/sprite.json` returns 200, `…/sprite.png` returns 200, and CORS headers allow your domain.
Open the JSON and search for `us-interstate_2`, `road_3`, etc.
After `map.on('load')`, run `map.hasImage('us-interstate_2')`. If `false`, the sprite is missing that ID.
Look for `Image ""us-interstate_2"" could not be loaded` (fired by `styleimagemissing`).
Verify the badge PNG request is actually happening (if you are using `addImage` or the resolver).

## 5. Putting it all together – a minimal, production-ready solution

Below is a **complete example** that works with any OpenMapTiles style (Bright, Liberty, or a custom one) **without editing the style’s layers**. It adds a second sprite sheet that contains only the shield badges; the rest of the style continues to use its original sprite.
```json
/* style.json (only the root part that changes) */
""version"": 8,
""sprite"": [
{ ""id"": ""default"", ""url"": ""https://my.cdn.com/tiles/my-icons/sprite"" },
{ ""id"": ""osm-shields"", ""url"": ""https://my.cdn.com/tiles/osm-shields/sprite"" }
/* … the rest of the style stays exactly as you got it … */
*Steps to create `osm-shields` sprite*
1. Clone the official OSM Bright sprite repo:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style.git
cd osm-bright-gl-style/sprite
2. The directory already contains `sprite.png`, `sprite.json`, and `@2x` variants – they include **all US shield IDs** listed above.
3. Upload the whole directory to your CDN (preserve the filenames).
*Result*: The map now finds `us-interstate_2`, `road_3`, etc. automatically, and the shields render with their badges. No layer code changes are required.
